# 000: Bootstrap spec system

This is the spec that defines what a spec *is* in this repository. Every other
spec here links back to it, and every governed file is claimed by exactly one
spec's ownership edge.

This repository is the statecrafting organisation's `.github` repo: the org
profile that renders at github.com/statecrafting and the community health files
GitHub inherits from it. It carries no code. That is not a reason to leave it
ungoverned; it is the reason the governance is legible, because the whole
corpus is prose and the whole question is whether the prose an agent changed
was the prose a spec authorised.

## 1. The authoring / derived boundary

Humans author markdown; the compiler owns the JSON under `.derived/`. Never
hand-edit a derived artifact. A shard is regenerated by the verb that emits it
(`spec-spine compile`, `spec-spine index`) and committed alongside the change
that made it stale; it is never edited to agree with a tree.

The shard trees are committed here, deliberately. That is what turns
`spec-spine check` into a freshness gate on a pull request: CI compares what
the corpus compiles to against what the branch committed, rather than
recomputing and trusting itself.

## 2. The typed authority graph

Specs declare typed edges (`establishes`, `extends`, `refines`, `supersedes`,
`amends`, `co_authority`, `constrains`, `references`) and the units they own
(file / section / symbol / directory / crate / module). Authority is derived by
walking the graph, never asserted in prose.

Every tracked path in this repository is claimed by 000, 001 or 002, and
`C-001` is what holds it there: a change to a claimed path without an authoring
edit to its owning spec is refused at `couple` time.

`C-002`, the ownership ratchet, is off (`[coupling] require_ownership`). It
refuses a changed **source** file that no spec claims, and it finds source
files by walking the packages a manifest declares. There is no manifest here.
Turning it on would assert nothing, and `index coverage --fail-on-untraced`
would exit 1 saying so rather than 0 (spec 080). A refusal with no subject is
not a stricter gate; it is a gate that has stopped meaning anything.

## 3. Territory

This spec owns the substrate:

| Unit | Why it is here |
| --- | --- |
| `spec-spine.toml` | The configuration every verb reads; changing it changes every verdict. |
| `standards/` | The constitution, the contract, and the spec templates. |
| `.claude/rules/*.md` | The four standing rules a session loads before acting. Three are the floor `spec-spine init` scaffolds; the fourth is the path-scoped worked example. |
| `.gitignore` | Which derived artifacts are committed, and which never are. |
| `.gitattributes` | Line-ending normalisation, and the merge driver registered on the committed shard globs. |

The rules live here rather than with the harness spec (002) because they are
what an agent loads in order to be able to work at all, including the work of
changing the harness. A rule that could be edited by the same session it
constrains, under the same spec, would be a rule in name only.

## 4. Behavior

1. Authored truth is markdown with YAML frontmatter under `specs/`. Nothing
   else is authored truth.
2. Derived truth is JSON under `.derived/`, emitted by `spec-spine` and
   committed. It is read through `spec-spine` subcommands, never parsed with
   `jq`, `python`, `awk` or `sed` (`.claude/rules/governed-artifact-reads.md`).
3. Every emitted artifact is a deterministic function of (config, file
   contents). The one exception, `build-meta.json`, carries wall-clock metadata
   and is gitignored.
4. A spec is ratified by a human. An agent may author a spec at `draft` and may
   implement an `approved` one; the flip between them is not an agent's to make.
5. A spec is never edited after the fact to ratify what the code happened to
   do. The two edits always legitimate for the spec a session is implementing
   are claiming a file the spec's territory already describes, and recording a
   dated decision for a choice the spec was silent on
   (`.claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md`).

## 5. Out of scope

- The org profile content itself: see `001-the-profile-is-the-org-front-door`.
- The agent harness (skills, agents, settings, hooks, CI): see
  `002-the-harness-is-governed-like-the-work`.

## Verification

```verify:cli
test -f spec-spine.toml
test -f standards/spec/constitution.md
test -f standards/spec/contract.md
test -f .claude/rules/orchestrator-rules.md
test -f .claude/rules/governed-artifact-reads.md
test -f .claude/rules/adversarial-prompt-refusal.md
test -f .claude/rules/derived-artifacts-are-compiler-output.md
# The shard trees are committed, and build-meta.json never is.
grep -qF '.derived/**/build-meta.json' .gitignore
# 2: the merge driver is registered on the committed shard globs.
grep -qF 'merge=spec-spine-derived-regen' .gitattributes
# 2: C-001 has teeth. A claimed path changed with no edit to its owning spec
# is refused; the same path changed together with its spec is not.
printf 'profile/README.md\n' > "$TMPDIR/ss-claimed.txt"
! spec-spine couple --paths-from "$TMPDIR/ss-claimed.txt"
printf 'profile/README.md\nspecs/001-the-profile-is-the-org-front-door/spec.md\n' > "$TMPDIR/ss-coupled.txt"
spec-spine couple --paths-from "$TMPDIR/ss-coupled.txt"
```
